elements.id-string-3: \title{Application and analysis of MUSIC algorithm for anomaly detection in microwave imaging without a switching device}\author{Won-Kwang Park}\ead{parkwk@kookmin.ac.kr}\address{Department of Information Security, Cryptology, and Mathematics, Kookmin University, Seoul, 02707, Korea.}
elements.id-string-5: Although the MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm has demonstrated suitability as a microwave imaging technique for detecting anomalies, there is a fundamental limit that it requires a switching device to be used which permits an antenna to transmit and receive signals simultaneously.
elements.id-string-6: In this paper, we design a MUSIC-type imaging function using scattering parameter data to find small anomaly and explore its mathematical structure.
elements.id-string-7: Considering the investigated structure, we confirm that the imaging performance is highly dependent on the antenna configurations and suggest an arrangement of antennas to enhance imaging performance.
elements.id-string-8: Simulation results with synthetic data are displayed to support theoretical result.
elements.id-string-11: Microwave imaging \sep MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) \sep Scattering parameter data \sep Simulation results \sep Switching device
elements.id-string-13: Retrieving of unknown targets from scattered field or scattering parameter data in multi-static measurement environment has been of great interest for many years in both inverse scattering problem and microwave imaging due to its various potential applications such as non-destructive evaluation \cite{CMPD,FMGD,TLRD}, biomedical imaging \cite{A2,CJGT,ML2}, radar imaging \cite{JBRBTFC,LSL,SSA}.
elements.id-string-14: To this ends, various reconstruction algorithms have been proposed and they are classified as iterative (or quantitative) and non-iterative (or qualitative) methods.
elements.id-string-15: We refer to remarkable researches \cite{AGJKLSW,BCS,C7,CK,DL,SH,Z2} for the description of various iterative and non-iterative techniques in both inverse scattering problems and microwave imaging.
elements.id-string-16: MUltiple SIgnal Classification (MUSIC) algorithm is a well-known,  promising qualitative method in both inverse scattering problem and microwave imaging.
elements.id-string-17: From the pioneering research by Devaney \cite{D}, MUSIC was successfully applied for identifying point-like scatterers in multi-static measurement data.
elements.id-string-18: After the successful application, it has been applied various inverse scattering problems such as identification of two- and three-dimensional small targets \cite{AILP,ZC}, fast imaging of crack-like defects \cite{P-MUSIC1,P-MUSIC8}, detection of internal corrosion \cite{AKKLV}, imaging of buried targets \cite{AIL1,G2}, limited-aperture and limited-view problems \cite{AJP,P-MUSIC7} as well as microwave imaging such as damage assessment for intricate structures \cite{BYG}, through-the-wall radar imaging \cite{CPPPDT}, time-reversal imaging \cite{MGS}, radar imaging \cite{OBP}, anomaly detection from scattering matrix \cite{P-MUSIC6}, breast cancer detection \cite{RSCGBA}, and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging \cite{ZZK}.
elements.id-string-19: Let us emphasize that for a successful application of MUSIC in microwave imaging, the generated scattering matrix whose elements are scattering parameters must be symmetric.
elements.id-string-20: If the matrix is non-symmetric, it is impossible to apply the MUSIC directly.
elements.id-string-21: Due to this reason, most of researches has been performed with the strong assumption that the antenna can transmit and receive signals, i.e., switching devices can be used.
elements.id-string-22: However, the issue of microwave imaging without a switching device may also exist as a result of limited system configurations.
elements.id-string-23: In this paper, we consider the application of MUSIC algorithm for identifying small anomaly from measured scattering parameter data at a fixed frequency when the switching device is not available.
elements.id-string-24: To this end, we assume that the scattering matrix is non-symmetric, design a new imaging function of MUSIC based on the structure of left- and right-singular vectors associated with nonzero singular values of the scattering matrix, and show that it can be represented by an infinite series of Bessel functions and antenna arrangements.
elements.id-string-25: This is based on the application of the Born approximation and integral equation formula for the scattering parameter in the existence of a small anomaly.
elements.id-string-26: Based on the theoretical result, we confirm that the imaging performance of proposed MUSIC is significantly dependent on the total number and location of transmitting and receiving antennas.
elements.id-string-27: To support the theoretical result, various simulation results with synthetic and experimental data are exhibited.
elements.id-string-28: It is worth to mention that if the total number of transmitting and receiving antennas is sufficiently large, it is possible to obtain a good result via MUSIC.
elements.id-string-29: However, in real-world microwave imaging applications, increasing total number of antennas somehow difficult.
elements.id-string-30: Instead of increasing total number of antennas, we investigate a method of arranging the antennas for obtaining a better result based on the elimination of unnecessary extra terms  that disturb the detection in the imaging function.
elements.id-string-31: The rest of this paper is organized as follows.
elements.id-string-32: In Section \ref{sec:2}, we briefly survey the basic concept of scattering parameters and MUSIC algorithm without switching devices.
elements.id-string-33: In Section \ref{sec:3}, we prove that the imaging function can be expressed as an infinite series of Bessel functions and the antenna arrangement.
elements.id-string-34: Sections \ref{sec:4} and \ref{sec:5} present a set of simulation results with various antenna arrangements from synthetic and experimental data, respectively.
elements.id-string-35: Section \ref{sec:6} provides short conclusion and perspective of this study.
